source_refs.note: Endotherms: a main subheading of 13.3.1 Types of Animals on the basis of Heat Source, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 7-8.

blocks.text: Endotherms generate the majority of their body heat through internal metabolism. They maintain a relatively constant body temperature, often higher than the environment. Birds and mammals are endotherms. When it gets cold, they may shiver (muscle contractions) or burn brown adipose tissue for heat. Most endotherms have insulation to retain heat such as hair, feathers, or fat.
